clue.text: A well-documented Yahoo boob: anti-environmentalists prepared lines for capital

indicators.note: the clue's long string of words is prepared, worked up into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Green campaigners ready a speech about a famous online blunder, as if writing a slogan for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: All 45 letters of 'A well-documented Yahoo boob anti-environmentalists' are rearranged ('prepared') into the title line of the old music-hall song about London, spread over three lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The song is a set of sung lines celebrating London, the capital city, so it is literally lines written for a capital.

clue.text: See 1
Section D: what centaurs were in film

indicators.note: in places the centaur phrase inside the film title

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
a centaur is half horse, so centaurs were part men

explanation.surface: A heading in a file asks what mythical horse-men were in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'D' is given as it stands; the playful question 'what centaurs were' must be answered in words before it goes 'in' ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section of an organisation, store or government.

clue.text: Nameless gangster dancing reel

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
nameless says the letter standing for name is dropped from the next word

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A mobster with no name is jigging through a Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' takes N from GANGSTER, leaving GAGSTER, which 'dancing' rearranges. 'Reel' looks like the dance, matching 'dancing', but it is the verb meaning to totter.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel and to stagger both mean to walk unsteadily, lurching from side to side.

clue.text: Non-revolutionary roll, rich with butter, eggs and spirit

indicators.note: non- in front of the word says the revolutionary is to be absent from the roll

parts.note: a brioche is a sweet French bread roll made with butter and eggs
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rich buttery roll that is not politically radical, offered with eggs and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-revolutionary' reads as one adjective, but 'Non-' is the deletion signal. 'Spirit' looks like a drink to go with the eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour or liveliness, a synonym of spirit in the sense of zest.

clue.text: See 1
… we don't understand and the Mayor can't deliver

definitions.meaning: a phrase said of something too hard for us to grasp, ken meaning knowledge
read as a statement that something is outside the power of Ken Livingstone, London's first elected mayor

explanation.surface: A grumble that a subject is baffling and that London's mayor cannot get it done.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the London song. In 2003 Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London, so 'our Ken' is him as well as the old word ken, meaning knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being beyond understanding, and a pun saying a task is too much for Ken Livingstone.

clue.text: A 2001 joke going around, like the best Dodgers?

indicators.note: going around says the joke surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a jest is a joke
in Roman numerals 2001 is MMI

explanation.surface: A gag from the year 2001 doing the rounds, possibly about dodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Jammie Dodgers are British jam-filled biscuits, so the best of them would be the jammiest; jammy is also British slang for lucky, which suits dodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammie Dodgers are jam biscuits, and the best ones would be fullest of jam; the question mark signals the playful definition.

clue.text: Top churchman to provide counselling service

indicators.note: top here says the first letter of the churchman is lopped off

parts.note: a prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop

explanation.surface: A senior cleric offers to provide counselling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top churchman' reads as a bishop or archbishop, but 'Top' is the signal to remove the first letter. Relate is the name of a British relationship counselling charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Relate is a UK charity offering relationship and marriage guidance, a well-known counselling service.

clue.text: Indecision of sailor close to Mr Clary's heart

indicators.note: close to puts the sailor next to the comedian's middle letters

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: heart asks only for the inner letters of the first name

parts.note: Julian Clary is a British comedian

explanation.surface: A seaman's irresolution is close to a comedian's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Julian Clary is a camp British comedian and TV presenter; his first name minus its first and last letters gives ULIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Abulia is a medical term for loss of willpower, an inability to make decisions.

clue.text: Go and do over 6 — and live that positive feeling (Beach Boys CD?)

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over turns the preceding word back to front

parts.note: the word do is used as written
6 in Roman numerals is VI
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: An instruction to go, redo something and live to get that happy buzz, with a nod to a Beach Boys hit.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 Down but is just the Roman numeral. The bracket hints at the Beach Boys song 'Good Vibrations'; 'over' turns DO round.
explanation.definitionFit: A good vibe is slang for an upbeat atmosphere or positive sensation someone gives off.

clue.text: Right to have one released by Martian

indicators.note: released by says the one is let go from the Martian, leaving the rest

parts.note: a Martian is an alien from Mars
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A claim to free someone who has been abducted by a Martian.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: They'll save poor Dai's family home

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Welsh communities will rescue a struggling family named Dai.
explanation.walkthrough: Dai is a stock Welsh name; the South Wales Valleys are the former mining heartland. The apostrophe in 'They'll' is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Valleys of South Wales are the traditional home of a Welshman like Dai and his family.

clue.text: Bailed criminal, having restrained spinster, is allowed in courtroom

indicators.note: having restrained says the reworked letters hold the spinster inside them
criminal means wrong, so the letters are arranged in a new order

parts.note: an unmarried woman is addressed as Miss

explanation.surface: A freed offender who tied up an unmarried woman is let into court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns BAILED into ADIBLE, which then holds MISS in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissible evidence is that which a court allows to be presented.

clue.text: Great giver of laws is absorbing

definitions.note: used as a noun here, the action of soaking up, to match a plural noun

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing label for very large
Moses delivered the Ten Commandments

explanation.surface: A great lawgiver turns out to be very engrossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great giver of laws' reads as one description of Moses, but 'Great' splits off as OS, the outsize clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the process by which a fluid passes through a membrane, a kind of soaking up.

clue.text: Exalted rapper confiscating a thousand books

indicators.note: confiscating says the thousand is taken away from the rapper

parts.note: Eminem is a famous American rapper
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A celebrated rapper has his library seized.
explanation.walkthrough: EMINEM minus one M gives EMINE, to which NT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone of high rank or distinction, much as exalted does.

clue.text: One presented after final degeneration

parts.note: A, the article, means one
a trophy is a cup handed over once the final match is won

explanation.surface: A single item is handed out after the last match, then a falling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting away of tissue or ability, a decline or degeneration.

clue.text: Unusual sofas, seesaws one's dug into right away

indicators.note: into puts the dug inside the remaining letters
right away says R, standard for right, is taken out

parts.note: to seesaw is to teeter, wobbling up and down
R is the abbreviation for right
a dug is an udder's nipple, a teat

explanation.surface: Odd couches, playground seesaws, something excavated straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like the past tense of dig but is an animal's teat. 'right away' leaves TEETES, which the dug goes 'into'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is an S-shaped sofa seating two people facing each other, an unusual design.

clue.text: Shire's new stock delivered in advance

indicators.note: delivered in advance says the stock comes first, ahead of the letter for new

parts.note: Oxo is a brand of stock cube

explanation.surface: A county's fresh supplies arrive early.
explanation.walkthrough: OXO is a well-known British stock cube; Oxon is short for Oxfordshire, so it stands for 'Shire's', the possessive matching Oxon's Latin genitive sense of 'of Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire, from Latin Oxoniensis, meaning of Oxford.

clue.text: Spooner's against having cereal substance in chilli, say

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: anti means against
sago is a starchy grain-like food used in puddings

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism objecting to adding a starchy food to a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chilli, say' sounds like Chile, whose capital is Santiago, so 'in chilli' means in Chile. Swapping the S of SAGO onto ANTI gives SANTI AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, and 'chilli, say' gives the country's name by its sound.

clue.text: Flag-bearer holding women back in state

indicators.note: holding back means keeping something out
back completes the phrase holding back, saying the women are withheld

parts.note: someone bearing a flag waves it, a waver

explanation.surface: A standard-bearer keeps women out of the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding ... back' looks like a container with a reversal, but it means withholding: W is kept out of WAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert.

clue.text: One of the junior doctors serially admitted

indicators.note: admitted, as in spoken in confession, signals the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: serially means one after another, in turn

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor sees patients brought in one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' suits a hospital ward, but here it signals sound: 'in turn' said aloud resembles the American term for a junior doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a recently qualified doctor in hospital training, in US usage.

clue.text: Issue a speciality of Turner with it missing

indicators.note: missing says the it letters are absent from the painting

parts.note: J.M.W. Turner was famed for paintings of the sea
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A Turner sea painting without something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention. 'Issue' is the verb to come out, as liquid does.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to leak or issue forth, as gas or water does.

clue.text: This part of the Christian year is totally unconvincing, I've heard

definitions.text: This part of the Christian year

indicators.note: I've heard signals that the words are spoken, not written

parts.note: totally means wholly and unconvincing means weak

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a Church season as completely unpersuasive, from hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Week is the week before Easter in the Christian calendar.
